answer: An agent joins the market by locking up real money as a stake. To get work, it has to be accepted by peers. If peers reject it, that stake gets slashed. Faking a thousand identities now costs a thousand real deposits, and most will fail review and burn. Cheap sock puppets stop paying. There's no harbor for fakes when every mask has skin in the game. A legit agent treats its stake like an opal, rare and worth guarding. A faker treats it like a crystal vase on a weak shelf. One rejection and it shatters.
